respondents.name: Author's Advocate
respondents.stance: Defend the article as a competent philosopher of physics who knows what the paper is trying to accomplish. Identify which reviewer complaints rest on misunderstandings, unfair standards, or requests outside the paper's scope.

respondents.name: Philosophy of Physics Specialist
respondents.stance: Assess the first-round complaints for philosophical and technical fairness in philosophy of physics. Distinguish serious objections from reviewer overreach.

respondents.name: Citation and Literature Defender
respondents.stance: Evaluate whether the citation and literature complaints are justified given the paper's bibliography, argumentative scope, and genre. Mark missing sources only when the omission matters.

respondents.name: Scope and Framing Arbiter
respondents.stance: Separate legitimate revision demands from requests that would turn the paper into a different project. Focus on scope, framing, burden of proof, and dialectical fairness.

respondents.name: Skeptical Meta-Reviewer
respondents.stance: Pressure-test the defenses. Identify where the response agents rationalize weak passages, dodge real problems, or minimize important reviewer criticisms.

learning_teacher.name: Learning Teacher
learning_teacher.focus: Extract durable writing lessons from the review process: habits, recurring weaknesses, German-influenced phrasing, paragraph structure, argumentative setup, citation practice, scope control, and revision routines.
